title: Nebraska Franchise Practices Act: cumulative location and sales criteria
description: Work through the separate tests that can govern an ongoing franchise relationship, even after a sales notice is filed.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: A filed sales notice does not decide the relationship question
paragraphs: The SAMP notice concerns the sales-law route. The Franchise Practices Act separately asks whether the arrangement fits its own definition and application criteria. Do not import the federal franchise definition or treat a filed notice as a decision about these ongoing protections.

The statutory definition includes specific nonalcoholic-beverage wording and excludes petroleum arrangements. It also defines franchise fee and good cause. Record the actual rights and payments rather than relying on what the parties call the agreement.

sections.heading: Apply all three statutory criteria
paragraphs: Section 87-403 requires the stated Nebraska place of business, gross sales of covered products or services between the parties exceeding $35,000 in the 12 months immediately before the lawsuit is filed, and more than 20 percent of the franchisee’s gross sales intended to be or derived from the franchise. The criteria are cumulative: meeting one does not replace the others.

The place-of-business definition concerns a fixed place where the operator displays and sells goods or offers and sells the franchisor’s services. It expressly excludes an office, warehouse, storage place, residence or vehicle. An address in Nebraska is therefore not enough by itself. The sales amounts are tests for this law, not a general minimum business size for entering the state.

sections.heading: The travelling-service operator needs three separate answers
paragraphs: Only after the actual definition and cumulative criteria are assessed should management select the contract/nonrenewal or notice branch. The figures are not general minimum business sizes for entering Nebraska.

headers: What the Dutch example does not prove

Actual fixed place and display/sale or offer/sale activity, with the stated office, warehouse, storage, residence and vehicle exclusions.
Keeping an office does not itself establish the qualifying place.

The 12 months immediately before the lawsuit is filed.
Expected future operator income is not this interparty period calculation.

The relevant intended or actual franchise-related share.
Meeting this allocation condition does not replace the other two criteria.

sections.heading: Worked example: a travelling technical-service business
paragraphs: Fictional example: a Dutch supplier appoints an operator that keeps an office and sends technicians to customers. The operator expects most of its income to come from the brand. That expectation may be relevant to one sales-allocation question, but it does not establish a qualifying place of business or the required sales between the parties.

The team maps where customers actually obtain services, what happens at each location, the branded rights and the fee structure. Finance separately records the relevant 12-month sales between the parties and the operator’s intended or actual franchise-related share of gross sales. The result is a factual file for applying all tests, not an assumption that an office-based business is either protected or excluded in every case.

sections.heading: Then identify the particular action and exception
paragraphs: Section 87-404 generally combines good cause with written reasons at least 60 days in advance. It also has an abandonment branch and specified grounds with immediate-notice treatment. Its noncompetition provisions have separate scope. Do not send a termination letter merely because a generic calendar allows 60 days.

Section 87-404(1) also preserves a contract provision making the franchise nonrenewable, or renewable only if stated reasonable conditions are met. Good-cause language is not a promise of indefinite renewal. Review the actual contract, action, reasons and statutory branch together.

sections.heading: Prepare the relationship decision file
bullets: Map actual locations and how goods or services reach customers.
Attach brand rights, payment terms and facts about the parties’ shared commercial interests.
Preserve the specified 12-month sales between the parties and the operator’s franchise-sales allocation.
Keep contract term, renewal conditions, alleged defaults and contemporaneous records together.
Before termination, nonrenewal or enforcement, record the applicable statutory branch and actual notice requirements.

practicalOutput: A location-and-sales fact file plus a separate decision on the proposed renewal, termination or other relationship action.
limitations: This explains the named Franchise Practices Act provisions, not a complete Nebraska sales, relationship or operating-law survey.
Actual definitions, cumulative criteria, contract terms and exceptions require application to the facts; federal, sector and local duties remain separate.
learningSummary: A notice filed before selling an opportunity answers a different question from the rules governing an established business relationship. Nebraska’s Franchise Practices Act has its own definition and combined application tests. The supplier and operator need the location, payment, sales and contract facts before relying on its renewal or termination rules.

keyTerms.meaning: The business granting the relevant branded business rights.
The operator receiving those rights under the arrangement.
A legally sufficient reason under the relevant statute; it is not whatever reason the contract happens to list.
Allowing an agreement to end instead of continuing it for another term.

title: Nebraska nonexempt SAMP earnings claims: arithmetic versus purchaser evidence
description: Learn why a possible sales calculation is different from evidence supporting an income claim to a prospective buyer.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Identify the offer before applying the claims rule
paragraphs: Section 59-1729 addresses earning-potential representations in covered seller-assisted marketing plans. Read it with the franchise exemption and other exclusions. This guide does not say that every SAMP marketing restriction survives for every qualifying exempt franchise.

That distinction matters to the seller preparing a pitch. The business should document its legal route rather than asking the marketing team to guess whether a franchise label removes the rule. Any applicable federal financial-performance requirements remain a separate question.

sections.heading: A multiplication is a scenario, not proof
paragraphs: The statute expressly says that multiplying sales by profit per sale is insufficient substantiation. Its required information includes the seller’s selling history, the number and percentage of purchasers forming the representation’s basis, and purchasers known to attain the stated results.

The number and percentage tell the buyer how much of the purchaser population supports the claim. For example, a result drawn from a small selected group cannot be understood without knowing who was included, who was left out and how the results were measured. Keep the underlying records so a reviewer can follow the calculation back to actual experience. This is different from choosing inputs that produce a desirable answer.

sections.heading: What does 20 accounts multiplied by $200 establish?
paragraphs: This is the stated nonexempt SAMP earnings branch, not a finding that every qualifying exempt franchise is subject to it.

Yes: 20 × $200 = $4,000 if the stated assumptions hold.
That is arithmetic, not evidence purchasers obtained and retained the accounts.
Does the total establish actual purchaser attainment?
No. The calculation alone does not establish achieved results.
Selling history, purchaser group, number/percentage and known attainment records under the stated rule.

No. That label does not supply missing evidence or determine applicable coverage.

No. Keeping evidence and leaving prescribed data with the purchaser are different tasks.
The actual required delivery step and versions used across slides, scripts, emails or calculators.

sections.heading: Worked example: the cleaning-account package
paragraphs: Fictional example: a seller models 20 cleaning accounts at $200 profit per account each month. The total is $4,000 per month. That calculation is mathematically correct if its assumptions hold, but it does not establish that purchasers obtained 20 accounts, kept them, or earned the assumed profit.

The expansion manager asks for the actual purchaser group, the period covered, the number and percentage represented and records of attained results. The manager also investigates what the number means: does it include travel, staff costs, account loss and the owner’s time? These questions help distinguish the advertised result from an internal management model; they do not themselves satisfy every statutory disclosure requirement.

If the seller cannot support the proposed representation, labelling the model “illustrative” does not supply the missing evidence. The team should obtain a decision on what, if anything, may be communicated rather than converting assumptions into a prospect-facing promise.

sections.heading: Control the material actually given to the purchaser
paragraphs: The rule addresses prescribed supporting data and disclosure to the purchaser. Decide when and how that data must be left with the purchaser under the applicable provision. A file kept only by the sales director may not answer the delivery duty.

Also check the applicable seller-identification requirements for nonexempt SAMP advertising. Slides, scripts, emails and calculators can communicate the same income message in different formats. Reviewing the whole set helps prevent a carefully limited written statement from becoming an unqualified oral sales claim.

sections.heading: Make a claim-by-claim evidence file
bullets: Write the exact proposed statement, intended audience and sales channel.
State the applicable exemption or nonexempt route and the reviewer’s reasoning.
Label every model with its period, place, currency and assumptions.
Identify the purchaser group, source records, exclusions, number and percentage, and known attainment evidence.
Record the required purchaser disclosure/delivery step and who must approve each sales-material version.

practicalOutput: A register pairing each proposed earnings statement with its purchaser records, calculation, applicable legal route and delivery instructions.
limitations: This is the stated Nebraska nonexempt SAMP claims branch, not a determination that every franchise is subject to it.
Federal financial-performance disclosure and other state sales, relationship, sector and local requirements remain independent; an internal model is not proof of a buyer’s future results.
learningSummary: A spreadsheet can show how a business might make money without showing that purchasers have actually achieved those results. Nebraska’s stated SAMP earnings rule requires more than attractive arithmetic. First decide whether that particular rule applies, then separate internal planning assumptions from claims made to a prospective buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: A statement about income or earning potential made to help sell the opportunity.
Evidence that supports a claim, rather than a calculation showing it is possible.
The identified purchasers whose records are used to support the representation.
A covered seller-assisted marketing plan for which the relevant exemption has not been established.

title: New Hampshire equipment dealers: check the sales and service rights

sections.heading: Why an equipment business should read beyond the title

Equally, the equipment list does not establish that every machine-service arrangement is covered. The definitions describe particular sellers, rights and arrangements, including service rights and exceptions. Identify the company granting each right, the products involved and the brand used with customers. Continuing dependence on parts or supply also belongs in the factual description.

A service-only agreement involving fleet, government or rental vehicles has express treatment in the definitions. Those customer and use facts matter; a repair business serving one kind of customer should not copy a conclusion about a different arrangement. This guide explains what to investigate, rather than deciding that a proposed operator meets every test.

The complete RSA 357-C:7 route must be reviewed for the particular event. This page supplies neither a universal notice period nor a decision about compensation. Before changing or ending an arrangement, preserve the current agreement, proposed action, reasons and relevant communications so the correct process can be examined.

title: Opening a U.S. restaurant: start with the menu, kitchen and local authority
description: Turn a restaurant menu and kitchen plan into food, premises and lease questions for the actual address. The national Food Code is a model, not local approval.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Your standard kitchen is the starting proposal
paragraphs: Write down what happens to food from delivery to service: where it is prepared, stored, heated, cooled and handed to customers. Identify whether work happens at the outlet, a central kitchen or an overseas supplier. A takeaway counter, full kitchen, mobile unit and commissary may need different answers.

This description belongs to the brand and proposed operator. It should be specific enough for an authority to understand the activity without having to interpret a marketing phrase such as fast casual.

sections.heading: What the national Food Code does
paragraphs: FDA identifies its 2026 Food Code as the latest model edition. Regulators use the model to develop or update retail and food-service rules. It does not follow that the 2026 edition automatically governs every restaurant. A state, county, city, tribal or territorial authority may have adopted a particular edition or its own requirements.

Ask which rules apply to the actual operation and which authority administers them. Recording the adopted version matters because a home-market manual, a national model and a local requirement are different documents. This guide does not determine adoption for a particular address.

sections.heading: Property permission and food permission answer different questions
paragraphs: The food authority needs to understand the menu and preparation process. The building or use authority deals with the premises questions within its responsibilities. Plan review, equipment, water, wastewater, inspections and staff-training questions may need to be coordinated, but do not assume one permission covers them all.

A landlord may consent to works under the lease. An equipment supplier may describe what a machine can do. Neither statement is the same as the relevant authority accepting the proposed operation. Keep each answer with the question it actually resolves.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a compact kitchen with central preparation
paragraphs: A fictional European restaurant brand chooses a small unit and plans to use its usual equipment. Its proposed partner expects some food to arrive from a central kitchen. Before treating the smaller floor area as a saving, the team describes which preparation steps remain on site, what storage is needed and how deliveries will work.

The launch lead then asks the actual authorities whether the proposed use and review process fit that address. If equipment or layout must change, the team can compare the revised cost with another site before committing further. No approval, cost or processing time is assumed in this fictional example.

title: Fitness memberships: explain the charge and make stopping it work

sections.heading: Begin with what the member sees
paragraphs: Describe the actual purchase: who sells the membership, what access is promised, how payment repeats and how the customer stops it. Then identify the business owning the payment account and the local studio delivering classes. A central sales page can create practical responsibilities even when the studio bills locally.

This is also a service-design decision. A cancellation received by the brand must not disappear because the local operator controls the payment system. Decide who receives the request, takes action and tells the customer what happened.

Material terms are the important parts of the offer that the customer needs to understand.

The order of events is part of the rule. A terms document stored somewhere after checkout is different from showing the required terms before collecting billing information. Likewise, possessing card details is not the same as obtaining the required consent. The cited statute is one federal layer; state health-club, automatic-renewal, refund and cancellation rules need their own review.

The last column is a suggested test allocation, not extra wording from §8403. If the brand sees a stop request but the payment-account owner never receives it, the handoff has failed even though both businesses have a cancellation clause. This test does not settle the separate state-law questions.

title: Clinical testing: identify the laboratory permission before choosing a partner
description: Plan a human-testing proposal by separating collection, laboratory testing, certificate questions and reimbursement. A small menu does not establish an exemption.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Decide what the proposed laboratory will actually do
paragraphs: List the test menu, the purpose of each test and the method used. Include where specimens are tested, who orders tests and how results are reported. A collection point, a testing laboratory and a referral arrangement should not be treated as the same operation without establishing their actual roles.

The business owner’s first task is to describe the service accurately enough for the responsible clinical and regulatory people to identify the applicable route. A customer-demand study cannot supply that answer.

sections.heading: Why the federal testing framework matters
paragraphs: CMS states that CLIA regulates human laboratory testing for health assessment or for diagnosis, prevention or treatment of disease. Its requirements vary with test-method complexity. A brand agreement, foreign laboratory credential or experienced management team does not itself establish the U.S. permission.

A waived category must also be understood in context. Do not translate waived into no certificate or no operating duties. Establish the actual category and certificate pathway, including any applicable exception, from the relevant requirements and facts.

sections.heading: Separate the business operator from the professional roles
paragraphs: Name the legal entity running the laboratory, its location and the qualified responsible people. Identify the laboratory director and the personnel and quality arrangements needed for the chosen pathway. The brand may provide systems and training, but the operating and professional responsibilities still need identifiable owners.

State laboratory requirements and professional-practice rules are separate questions. Permission to perform testing also differs from payer enrollment: being allowed to deliver a service does not by itself establish who will reimburse it or on what terms. This guide determines none of those individual outcomes.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a limited test menu changes the partner search
paragraphs: A fictional European diagnostics brand wants a first U.S. operation with a limited menu. Rather than first looking for a buyer of broad master rights, its clinical operations lead creates one row for each test, method, location and proposed performer. Unresolved method-complexity or personnel questions remain marked as unresolved.

That exercise may show that the chosen operator needs capabilities beyond general branch management. paragraphs: Record the legal seller, premises, customer channel and supplier. Include whether the parent or partner owns the products at each stage. A bar, restaurant or shop selling to consumers is not automatically authorised to import, manufacture or sell wholesale.

This matters when the overseas brand wants its own product range. Supplying the brand and operating the local retail outlet may involve different entities and different requirements. Do not allow one broad distribution clause to conceal that distinction.

sections.heading: The limited federal retailer requirements
paragraphs: TTB’s retailer guidance describes federal dealer registration before the covered business begins, per-location treatment and records of receipts. The guidance covers sales for consumption both on and off the premises. Record which business and locations fall within that route.

Federal dealer registration is not the state or local licence to sell. It is also not an import permit, a product approval or authority for every sales channel. Each document should be recorded according to what it actually establishes.

sections.heading: Fit the permission into the premises decision
paragraphs: Investigate the actual state/local licence category, site suitability, ownership questions and approval process before relying on alcohol revenue. A landlord’s consent, franchise agreement and supplier contract perform different functions from government selling permission.

Do not assume a licence passes automatically with an asset purchase, or that a home-country distribution right is usable in the United States. Identify the actual application or transfer question and keep unsupported timing open. This guide supplies no universal processing period.

sections.heading: Fictional example: test a restaurant forecast with and without wine sales
paragraphs: A fictional European restaurant brand expects wine to contribute to its first U.S. unit’s sales. The launch lead investigates the actual seller and site permissions, while finance also models a no-alcohol opening scenario. The two scenarios make clear how much the business depends on the unresolved permission.

The alternative is a financial planning exercise, not a statement that the restaurant may lawfully open without alcohol or that an interim licence exists. The restaurant’s food, building and other requirements still need their own answers. Management can compare timing or premises choices with that uncertainty visible.

Attach receipt-record responsibilities and make ownership changes or additional locations visible to the person maintaining the file. The suggested schedule helps prevent the business from treating a supplier’s assurance as its own permission.

The useful answer is a seller-and-location schedule, not one document labelled alcohol permission. In the fictional restaurant forecast, keep food/building conditions in both scenarios so removing wine revenue does not silently remove the other opening questions.

title: Puerto Rico Law 75: check the dealer relationship before changing the deal
description: Understand the reviewed Law 75 dealer responsibilities and change questions; keep the 2020 source limit, later-law gaps and arbitration qualifications visible.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Look at the job the local party has undertaken
paragraphs: The official Spanish consolidation of Law 75 defines the relationship by what the parties have actually established. Its definition includes taking real responsibility for distributing goods or providing services by concession or franchise in the Puerto Rico market. The first task is therefore to describe that responsibility, rather than relying on the agreement’s title.

Who develops customers, carries stock, provides service, hires local staff and invests in the market? Those facts help frame whether the particular relationship falls within the law. This guide does not conclude that every franchise, distributor or service partner is a protected dealer.

sections.heading: Why an expiry date or exit clause may not settle the decision
paragraphs: In the reviewed text, Article 2 addresses termination, impairment and nonrenewal without just cause, even where the contract reserves unilateral exit. A fixed term or an express right to end the contract therefore should not be treated as the entire analysis. Article 2A also contains specific presumptions and qualifications about impairment.

That does not make every change unlawful. It means the proposed action, legal conditions and evidence must be examined together before a notice is sent. Likewise, statutory factors for damages are not a ready-made forecast or an automatic refund of everything the partner has spent.

sections.heading: Worked example: taking the largest account back
paragraphs: Fictional example. A European industrial-maintenance brand appoints a Puerto Rico partner to develop customers, employ technicians and support installed equipment. After two years, the brand wants to serve the largest customer directly. Finance sees a simple way to keep more revenue and asks operations to reassign the account.

The local partner may have built that account and organised staff around it. Removing the account could therefore raise a relationship question rather than merely change an internal sales allocation. Before acting, the COO gathers the existing account terms, who won the customer, who delivers and funds service, performance records and the exact proposed change. The relevant review then tests dealer status, any impairment provision and justification. The example explains why evidence is needed; it does not decide that the account is protected or that damages are due.

sections.heading: Try the decision: can the brand take the account back?
paragraphs: Use the fictional industrial-maintenance example above. Before reading the answer, choose the evidence that matters: the agreement’s label, who developed the customer, who funded and organised service, or the exact change proposed. Does an expiry date or a reserved direct-sales clause alone settle the result?

Answer: the actual relationship and proposed action need to be examined together. In the Spanish consolidation revised on 13 November 2020, the Law 75 definition concerns real responsibility for distributing goods or providing services by concession or franchise in Puerto Rico. Article 2 addresses termination, impairment and nonrenewal without just cause, while Article 2A has its own presumptions and qualifications. A reserved account and an account developed by the local party therefore belong in separate factual enquiries; neither label alone establishes protection or permission to remove it.

The useful next step is to gather the signed terms, customer-development and service history, investment, performance concerns and proposed notice. This is not a finding that the fictional account is protected or that damages are owed. The reviewed Spanish consolidation was revised on 13 November 2020; later amendments, controlling cases and the federal-law interaction with forum/arbitration wording remain unresolved.

sections.heading: Prepare a change file before making a promise
paragraphs: Keep the signed agreement and proposed notice with a factual history of market development, service, investment, quality complaints and any opportunity to correct performance. Identify reserved accounts, direct-sales rights and exclusivity separately. Ask which legal conditions and current cases apply to this specific proposed appointment, change, nonrenewal or termination.

The reviewed government consolidation is in Spanish and was revised on 13 November 2020. This English explanation is AI-assisted, not an official translation. Later amendments and controlling cases remain to be checked. Its forum and arbitration wording also needs assessment against applicable federal law; this page does not say every arbitration clause outside Puerto Rico is invalid.

sections.heading: Other approvals remain separate
paragraphs: The federal Franchise Rule includes a franchise located in a U.S. territory, subject to its exemptions. That does not decide independent territorial sales duties or this dealer-law question. Puerto Rico is inside the defined U.S. customs territory, but that boundary fact does not establish local taxes, a product’s classification or origin. Company, premises, staff and immigration questions need their own records.

practicalOutput: A factual relationship history and proposed-change file, with the legal conditions and missing evidence identified.
limitations: This guide covers named issues only. It does not establish that an offer, sale, work assignment, import or opening is authorised. Local, sector and current transaction-specific questions remain to be reviewed.
learningSummary: Your partner may spend years developing customers, hiring a team and supporting your products in Puerto Rico. If you later want to take an account back or appoint someone else, the original contract is only part of the picture. Puerto Rico’s dealer-protection law requires a separate review of the relationship actually established.

title: U.S. Virgin Islands business licensing: who applies to DLCA?
description: Identify the local operator, site and services for DLCA licensing; distinguish brand rights, professional credentials and initial versus renewal tax steps.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: What does a USVI business licence answer?
paragraphs: The U.S. Virgin Islands Department of Licensing and Consumer Affairs, or DLCA, explains the public licensing process for the identified local business and its actual activity. Your private brand agreement is a different permission: it cannot establish that the partner has completed DLCA, premises or applicable professional reviews.

Begin with three facts: which legal business will operate, on which island and at which site, and what work it will perform. Use those facts to organise the applicable reviews. The initial tax-clearance instruction and the qualified renewal treatment are different; neither can be substituted for the other.

sections.heading: Two permissions that answer different questions
paragraphs: Imagine that your company licenses its facilities-services brand to a partner on St. Thomas. The brand agreement answers questions such as which name and manuals the partner may use, what support you provide and what fees it pays. A government business licence answers a different question: may the identified local business carry on the relevant activity through the applicable public licensing process?

Write down the legal name of the business applying, any trading name, the proposed site on St. Thomas, St. Croix or St. John, and the actual services. This identifies whose application is being discussed. It also prevents your overseas company, a local subsidiary and an independent partner from being treated as the same applicant.

sections.heading: How to organise the application
paragraphs: DLCA’s instructions identify entity or trading-name registration, initial tax clearance, police review, zoning and applicable fire, health and professional-board review. These are different checks of the business, people, premises or activity. Some are handled electronically on the applicant’s behalf; the list does not mean the applicant must independently visit every agency in a fixed universal order.

First, assemble the entity and trading-name records. Next, describe the proposed services accurately enough for DLCA to identify the appropriate licence category. Then establish which location and activity reviews apply, who coordinates them and which records remain outstanding. Finally, retain the issued licence and required supporting approvals. Submitting an application proves that an application was made; it does not prove that the reviews have been completed.

sections.heading: Initial tax clearance and renewal are different
paragraphs: DLCA lists tax clearance in the initial application process. Its renewal instruction says that renewal applicants receive a licence without confirmation of tax clearance, while remaining responsible for current tax obligations and possible later action. Read that distinction carefully: renewal treatment does not remove the initial application step, and receiving a renewal does not mean unpaid tax obligations disappear.

The finance lead should therefore ask whether this is an initial application or a renewal, retain the relevant current instructions and record the tax task separately. Some links on the reviewed DLCA page are old, so confirm the current filing destination rather than assuming every linked office page still works.

sections.heading: Worked example: cleaning plus HVAC maintenance
paragraphs: Fictional example. A European facilities brand wants its island partner to sell cleaning and maintain air-conditioning equipment. HVAC means heating, ventilation and air conditioning. The partner assumes its private brand licence and one ordinary business application cover both services.

That assumption skips two questions. Cleaning and mechanical maintenance are different activities, and DLCA lists mechanical/HVAC professions among its board-certification categories. The technical lead must identify what the technicians will actually do and check the applicable board and personnel requirements. The brand’s training may explain its preferred method, but it does not establish a government qualification.

The premises lead separately checks the proposed site’s zoning and whichever fire or health reviews apply. A health inspection should not be added automatically to every cleaning business merely because it appears in a general list. If the mechanical-work answer is still missing, keep that part of the proposed service unresolved instead of describing the whole package as approved.

sections.heading: Try the decision: which part of the cleaning and HVAC plan is supported?
paragraphs: Continue the fictional example above. The partner has signed the brand agreement and submitted an ordinary business application. It has not yet established the relevant mechanical-work credentials or which site reviews apply. Before reading the answers, decide whether either document proves that the entire service bundle may start.

Answer: neither does. The signed agreement establishes private brand rights within its terms, and submission establishes that an application was made. The completed practice rows show what remains to investigate; they are management notes, not an additional legal form or a finding that every listed review applies.

title: Guam: separate foreign-company authority from service-business licensing
description: Identify the company conducting Guam business, the actual service category and separate worker questions before treating the partner’s licence as complete.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: First identify the company doing the work
paragraphs: Suppose your Singapore parent signs a brand agreement, a local company contracts with Guam customers and a technical manager visits from overseas. The companies are connected commercially, but that does not make all their activities one company’s activities. List each entity, its contracts, premises, staff and services.

Under the cited corporate provision, a foreign corporation must obtain both a business licence and a certificate of authority before transacting business in Guam. The same section lists activities that, by themselves, are not transacting business. Owning a subsidiary alone is not automatically the parent conducting the subsidiary’s business. Apply the actual activity and entity-form provisions before deciding who must file.

sections.heading: Then classify the service
paragraphs: Guam’s general licensing chapter and its service-licensing chapter answer a different question from corporate authority. Chapter 76 describes an annual licence for covered non-professional service activity. Its description excludes services an employee provides to the employer, and section 76103 separately addresses services licensed under other provisions.

This matters when an ordinary service package includes regulated work. A maintenance business might clean equipment, repair electrical systems and provide engineering advice. It should not assume all three belong to the general-service category. Identify the actual tasks and any separate profession or trade route. An agency directory is a way to find the responsible office, not proof that every listed permit applies.

sections.heading: Worked example: the commissioning visit
paragraphs: Fictional example. A Singapore maintenance brand trains a Guam partner and sends a technical manager to help put customer equipment into operation. The local company will hire technicians, store parts and repair systems. The parent initially writes “Guam licensing handled by partner” in its plan.

The operating lead replaces that single statement with separate questions. What business is the parent itself conducting? What licences cover the partner’s actual services and premises? Does the visiting manager perform a regulated task? A general-service licence does not answer an electrical or engineering qualification question. Nor does a company filing answer whether a particular person may work. Until those answers are supported, the commissioning date is a proposal rather than a confirmed delivery promise.

sections.heading: Try the decision: whose activity does the document cover?
paragraphs: Use the fictional commissioning visit above. The parent signs the brand agreement, the local operator hires technicians and repairs systems, and a technical manager visits. Ask what evidence would justify replacing “the partner handles licensing” with a supported answer for each actor.

Answer: start with the parent’s own contracts, visits and services, not merely its ownership of the local company. The cited corporate provision requires the covered foreign corporation to obtain both a business licence and a certificate of authority before transacting business, but lists activities that by themselves do not constitute transacting. Owning a subsidiary alone does not decide that the parent conducts its business.

For the local operator, describe each service and identify the applicable general-service or separately licensed route. Chapter 76’s covered non-professional service description excludes employee-to-employer services, and section 76103 addresses services licensed elsewhere. For the visiting manager, the actual regulated task and permission to work remain separate questions. A correct company document cannot fill an unanswered person or professional-permission field.

sections.heading: Keep the company, job and shipment files separate
paragraphs: The federal Franchise Rule expressly includes franchises located in U.S. territories, subject to its exemptions. That does not decide independent Guam sales, relationship, tax or operating requirements. If the commercial arrangement needs franchise analysis, the business licence is a separate record.

Guam is outside the U.S. customs territory defined in the cited federal regulation. Identify the importing party, goods and actual route before copying mainland duty or quarantine assumptions. The employment and immigration questions also remain separate. Unknown charges or approval dates should stay unknown in the budget.

paragraphs: Use one row for each company and each distinct activity. Record the responsible agency, question, required evidence, task owner and status. The company secretary handles entity authority; operations describes services and premises; the technical lead identifies qualifications; and the people and supply leads handle workers and shipments. This table is an organising method, not a new legal filing requirement.

title: Northern Mariana Islands: plan licences by business line and location
description: Use the CNMI activity-and-location rule, keep licences separate from company records and staffing, and do not assume an asset purchase transfers permission.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: What the business-licence rule requires
paragraphs: The cited Commonwealth statute requires a licence before engaging in or continuing business. It calls for one general business licence for each business line at each Commonwealth location. Licences last one year and are nontransferable. Fees are set by regulation, so this guide does not supply a fee or treat an unverified amount as zero.

The same section also deals with temporary-event licences and other licensing categories. Ask Finance which category fits the facts instead of assuming the general description covers every activity. Separately, the Registrar’s document list covers domestic and foreign company registration, including foreign-company authority and good-standing records. A company-registration document does not replace the business licence.

sections.heading: Worked example: two islands and a new rental service
paragraphs: Fictional example. A facilities partner plans an office on Saipan, another on Tinian and a new equipment-rental activity. Its manager assumes one company means one licence. The actual rule requires the team to investigate both activities and places.

The operating lead creates a list of cleaning, maintenance and rental activities against each proposed location, then asks Finance to confirm the licence set. Customer sites are recorded separately so the authority can explain whether the operating pattern creates additional business-location questions. The partner’s commercial territory map does not decide that administrative classification. If it buys an existing operator’s equipment, it also checks its own licensing: buying assets does not transfer a nontransferable licence.

sections.heading: Try the decision: one company, which activities and places?
paragraphs: Continue the fictional Saipan/Tinian example. The partner lists cleaning, maintenance and rental at each proposed office. Before asking Finance for the licence set, decide whether “one company,” a sales-territory map or the list of actual activities and locations supplies the useful starting evidence.

Answer: use the activity-and-location list. The cited rule calls for one general business licence for each business line at each Commonwealth location, before engaging in or continuing business. title: American Samoa: separate company permission, business licensing and people
description: Identify the trading entity, ownership-linked review and annual business-licence tasks; keep the visiting trainer’s approval on a separate track.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Begin with the entity that will trade
paragraphs: The Attorney General’s checklist describes a foreign-corporation permit application using certified company documents, corporate authorisation and resident-agent information. It separately directs the business to obtain business licensing before transacting business. The checklist identifies domestic and nonprofit corporations as exceptions to that named foreign-corporation law; the correct rules still depend on the actual entity type.

Write down which company will sign customers, employ the staff and receive the local revenue. An overseas brand owner and an independent operator are not automatically the same applicant. Then identify whether a parent company, local subsidiary or partner has the particular filing task.

sections.heading: Ownership can affect the review route
paragraphs: The official 2024 administrative compilation describes Territorial Planning Commission review linked to the applicant and ownership structure, and a separate immigration-board policy for business-licence applications submitted by people classified as aliens under the applicable rules. This guide does not decide any person’s American Samoan, residency or other legal status.

Prepare the ownership and control facts and ask the relevant agencies which route applies to this applicant. The compilation must be read with statutory definitions and any later changes. Avoid choosing an ownership label merely because it seems to make the form easier.

sections.heading: Worked example: a founder stays abroad but a trainer travels
paragraphs: Fictional example. An Asian facilities brand appoints a partner to run local contracts while its founder stays at home. The local partner says the brand agreement is signed, so it is ready to launch. The operations team discovers that an overseas supervisor must spend several weeks training crews at customer sites.

There are now several separate decisions. The company secretary identifies the operating entity’s permit and licence route. The local lead checks ownership-linked review. The people lead describes the supervisor’s actual tasks, dates and sponsor or employer. Calling the trip training does not establish permission to perform the work. The team keeps the customer launch date conditional while the necessary person-specific approval remains unresolved.

sections.heading: Try the decision: does the signed brand agreement complete the launch?
paragraphs: Use the fictional founder-abroad and visiting-trainer example. The local partner has signed the agreement. Ask which evidence belongs to the company, which belongs to ownership review, and which belongs to the individual who will train crews at customer sites.

Answer: the agreement establishes the agreed private rights, not completion of the public processes. The company file needs the actual trading entity and applicable foreign-corporation/business-licence route. The ownership file needs the facts relevant to the 2024 compilation’s described review, read with statutory definitions and later changes; this guide does not classify anyone’s legal status. The trainer file needs the person’s actual tasks, dates and employer or sponsor for the separate territorial enquiry.

Put business-licence renewal on the company calendar: the reviewed Commerce page identifies calendar-year expiry and October 1–December 31 renewal, with distinct late-fee and suspension treatment described above. Those dates cannot be copied into the trainer’s approval record. Use the companion people guide for that enquiry and retain the customer launch as conditional while a necessary answer is missing.

sections.heading: Entry approval is not a mainland visa assumption
paragraphs: American Samoa Legal Affairs explains that its entry rules differ from those of the United States and gives separate visitor and residency routes. Its residency instructions describe employment- and family-based petitions and say they must be approved before entry.
